PullRequest.Title: sessions: address #335583 review feedback on ActionList hover panels
PullRequest.Body:
Follow-up to #335583, addressing the review threads that were left unresolved when that PR merged.

## What's fixed

- **Focus lost on live refresh**: `chatDropdownPill` now preserves the focused dropdown entry (and its open hover) across `updateItems()` refreshes triggered by live PR/CI/issue updates, instead of dropping focus back to the trigger control.
- **Narrow/phone viewport overflow**: `ActionListWidget`'s submenu-panel layout now clamps panel width and position to the viewport, so the hover panel stays fully on-screen even when neither side has room next to a narrow dropdown anchor (tested at 320px/375px).
- **Modified Tab captured**: the panel keydown handler now ignores `Tab` when `Ctrl`/`Meta`/`Alt` is held, so shortcuts like editor-group navigation bubble to the keybinding service instead of being treated as panel traversal.
- **Issue entries missing lifecycle state**: issue reference entries now get an `ariaDescription` with their lifecycle state (Open/Closed/Duplicate/Not planned), matching the existing behavior for pull requests.
- **Stale panel position after content grows**: `tabThroughPanel` hovers (used by GitHub reference cards) now also participate in resize observation, so the panel repositions itself (not just the focused row) when focusing a control reveals bounded text and grows the panel's height.
- **Draft PR CI over-polling**: `GitHubPullRequestPollingContribution` now only continuously polls CI checks for a draft pull request while its session is active; other open drafts refresh once instead of polling every 60 seconds.

## Testing

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/actionList.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionChatInputToolbar.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/github/test/browser/githubContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/chatPills.test.ts` — 138 passing
- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean

New regression tests cover: modified-Tab bubbling, panel width/position clamping at 320px/375px, panel repositioning when tabThroughPanel content grows (including near the viewport bottom), issue `ariaDescription` per lifecycle state, focus/hover preservation across dropdown refresh, and draft PR CI polling scoped to the active session.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Unconditional per-session CI polling kept every inactive open draft PR on a 60-second network refresh loop, so background request volume scaled with the number of distinct inactive draft PRs tracked by the sessions contribution.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Continuous GitHub check-runs API traffic and associated response processing for inactive draft sessions whose CI status was not being displayed.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: For an open draft PR, the contribution still performs one initial status refresh, but it registers the 60-second CI poller only while that draft's session is active. Inactive draft models therefore stop generating recurring GitHub check-runs requests, while non-drafts retain the previous polling behavior. Shared model references and refresh-promise coalescing preserve deduplication for duplicate keys and simultaneous refreshes.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 288 unconditionally registered GitHubPullRequestCIModel.startPolling() for every open PR after the status autorun acquired its CI model. GitHubPullRequestCIModel schedules one refresh every 60 seconds, and each refresh reaches GitHubPRCIFetcher.getCheckRuns(), which issues a GET to /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs. The contribution iterates every tracked session and PR identity, so inactive draft sessions generated one recurring request per distinct draft PR. The changed draft branch now observes active-session state and only owns startPolling() while that session is active; the added test proves inactive drafts receive the one initial refresh but zero polling registrations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and interact with an ActionList tab-through hover panel, including content growth and narrow mobile viewports
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the hover synchronously constructs its DOM, measures the list/row/panel rectangles, and writes the final panel width/position before display. Later content-size changes are delivered by the browser ResizeObserver and synchronously rerun layout; this observer work is on the visual update path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one observed open hover per widget; cost scales with genuine size changes of that panel, not total list length or all hidden hovers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One submenu can be open per ActionListWidget. Native ResizeObserver delivery batches size notifications; the callback runs serially on the UI thread, and disposal is tied to the current submenu's disposable store.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No external cache is involved. Geometry is recomputed for the one open panel when it opens or its observed border box changes; no hidden panels are observed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed condition adds one ResizeObserver only for the currently open tabThroughPanel, and the callback's geometry reads/writes are directly visible in layout().
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual panel DOM complexity and resize frequency vary, but realistic GitHub reference cards change size only on focus/content updates, not per frame.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added synchronous layout work is bounded to one visible panel and only runs on size changes needed to reposition it; width clamping may cause one follow-up observer delivery but does not establish a sustained layout loop.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh an open chat pill dropdown after live pull-request, CI, issue, or artifact data changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The observable autorun rebuilds flattened dropdown items, reads the current focused row, updates the existing virtualized list, and, only when a hover is open and reusable, measures the old/new focused row to animate movement. This UI work runs after data arrives and is on the visible dropdown refresh path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Upstream GitHub PR/issue/CI model refreshes populate the observables that can trigger the dropdown update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one model refresh per distinct shared model key at a time; dropdown rebuilding is one pass over the effective entries for each resulting observable change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same upstream model refreshes already drove dropdown item updates; the diff changes focus/hover preservation and optional row animation only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The network refresh completes before the observable UI update; the changed dropdown code itself performs no network request and does not move that request onto the rendering critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective visible section-entry count after grouping; one update per observable change, with only the focused/open-hover row eligible for animation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable reactions and DOM updates are serialized on the UI thread. Item-move animation ownership uses a mutable disposable so a later animation cancels the previous one.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GitHub service references share models by repository/PR/head key, refresh promises coalesce concurrent non-forced requests, and ETags avoid replacing unchanged data. The dropdown itself performs no long-lived caching and rebuilds only the current sections.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added work is an O(1) focus lookup plus an existing O(n) list rebuild; extra O(n) hover matching and two geometry reads occur only while a reusable hover is open.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Entry counts and live update rates vary, but session artifact/reference lists are bounded user-visible collections and CI polling is normally minute-scale.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra visible-refresh work is bounded and infrequent, while no expensive boundary was added or multiplied.

Scenarios.Scenario: Track GitHub CI status for active and inactive draft pull-request sessions after workbench restore
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session/PR identity resolution acquires a shared PR model and performs the existing PR refresh. Once an open draft resolves, one CI refresh fetches current checks; recurring CI refreshes are off the immediate startup critical path and now run only while that draft's session is active.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET pull-request details and reviews for each tracked PR model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced refresh per distinct repository/PR model initially and then per its existing 60-second PR poll schedule; shared references deduplicate duplicate session references to the same key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical PR-model refresh and polling behavior existed before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial refresh is required to determine whether the PR is open/draft and precedes CI scheduling; recurring calls are background work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial coalesced CI refresh per distinct open draft head. After the diff, only the active draft continues at one request per 60-second cycle; inactive drafts have zero recurring CI poll requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, every distinct inactive open draft head also retained a poll client and issued a check-runs request every 60 seconds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial call populates status; recurring polling is background and does not block session interaction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct inactive open draft PR heads after shared-key deduplication; active drafts remain one poller per distinct key.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: PR and CI models serialize/coalesce refreshes per shared key, while distinct PR keys have independent poll schedulers and no global limiter. The diff removes inactive-draft poll clients, reducing aggregate independent network concurrency at each interval.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CI models are shared by owner/repo/PR/head SHA, concurrent refresh calls return the same in-flight promise, and subsequent requests carry an ETag. A head change creates a new key; inactive drafts receive no negative-cache loop beyond the existing initial refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the old unconditional startPolling call, model scheduler interval, concrete REST endpoint, active-session gate, and regression test call counts establish the mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of inactive draft sessions per user is variable, but the removed request rate is exactly one CI poll cycle per distinct inactive draft model every 60 seconds.
Scenarios.Verdict: This PR fixes a concrete boundary-fanout regression by eliminating recurring CI requests for inactive drafts. The fix was recorded with its blamed introducing commit; it does not warrant a review finding against this PR.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rebuild issue pill entries with lifecycle-state aria descriptions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The derived issue-section builder maps the currently resolved issue references and computes one localized status label and URI string per entry before rendering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of issue references in the current session, one status lookup/string per entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous observable recomputation on the UI thread; no queue, worker, or parallel boundary is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or retained lifecycle is introduced; descriptions live with the same ephemeral entry objects already rebuilt for each observable update.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added operation is directly visible and has no transitive I/O or heavyweight allocation path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Issue-entry counts vary by session, but the added constant string formatting per displayed issue is small relative to the pre-existing entry and hover construction.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; this is bounded linear string work within an already linear entry rebuild.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and relevant callers/models. No diff-introduced performance finding met the reporting threshold. The draft-CI change is a verified performance regression fix and was recorded via blame.
